chapter: George Lewis's first bands and instruments
title: First E-flat clarinet and an all-day parade
summary: George recalls playing E-flat clarinet for the first time on an all-day parade and how he got the instrument.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: But yeah, I learned there was another Eureka band in the early days in this band. Probably he was in that band. Might have been in that. But this band here, I'm telling you about this, it's the first time I ever played E-flat clarinet in my life. And we played the second to the last All Fellas Day Parade, which was all day parades. It started at nine o'clock in the morning and lasted five in the evening.
Was that the May the 10th parade? That is, May.

All day, last all day. We used to stop and rest at Espinade and Claiborne, sit in the grass and rest. And they gave a picnic at the fairground and they used a brass band out there and they used a band out in the field, what they called a hunky-tump. Out in the field where a lot of the women were afraid to go out there on account of the guy was grabbing and rake them and the thing out there on the field.

Yeah. Well, I used B-flat and I had E-flat clarinet in my pocket. Both of them on the parade, right? Yeah, the first E-flat clarinet I used, Landry was working as a sailor for a drum or a war line, and he got it for me as a trial. And I started playing it and Joe, also Joe Watson, not Watkins the drummer, Joe Watson, Watkins, who was playing with the Sam Morgan band. Well they had a band out, I didn't remember which band he was playing. It was the first time he ever used an E-flat clarinet, it was both of us that day. He couldn't use his and I used mine.
